title: Holding Several Road Hazard Protection Certificates
content:
A customer may hold any number of Road Hazard Protection certificates, one for each Crestline tire set they own. There is no limit on the number of certificates per customer: a household with three vehicles may carry three certificates, each of a different plan.

**Each certificate stands alone.** Certificates never pool with one another. The repairs, replacements, roadside calls and claim counts of one certificate are used and counted only on that certificate; a second certificate held by the same customer neither adds to nor draws on them.

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a ceiling on certificates per customer? | No; one per tire set owned, any number of sets. |
| Must the certificates be on the same plan? | No; each set's certificate may be of a different plan. |
| Can an unused roadside call on one certificate serve a vehicle on another? | No; calls do not pool between certificates. |
| Does a repair on one certificate count toward another certificate's claim limit? | No; claim counts do not pool. |

How many certificates a single tire set may carry is governed by the separate rule on one certificate per tire set.

*Hypothetical example.* A customer with a sedan and a pickup holds a 36-Month certificate on the sedan's set and a 12-Month certificate on the pickup's set. Two repairs booked on the sedan's certificate leave the pickup's certificate untouched.
